stories.headline: Create a reusable Agent Skill to audit app permissions before installation
stories.read_scope: Full official permission release covering narrowly scoped access, organizational approval and refresh-token changes.
stories.summary: GitHub added narrower App permissions for repository creation and installation expansion, alongside offline-access credential improvements. Those controls create a useful teaching case for an Agent Skill that inventories requested access without changing settings. The reusable procedure should compare current and proposed scopes, identify owner approvals, document token handling and stop when consequences remain unclear.
stories.why_it_matters: Before authorizing any integration, use a read-only permission review that lists data exposure, external actions and approval owners. Test both harmless and excessive requests, retain the report and require human sign-off. A Skill documents checks; it cannot grant assurance automatically.
stories.agent_skills_evidence: Reusable SKILL.md procedure based on GitHub October 13 original report. Inputs: requested app permissions and repository scope. First inventory read/write access; compare each capability against the actual task. Next identify owner-approval requirements and credential lifecycle. Then run two test cases: one necessary read-only scope and one excessive write scope. Return a structured permission table, supporting source links and PASS, REVIEW or STOP recommendation. Final action must be explicit human authorization; the Skill does not install software or alter permissions.
stories.image_alt_intent: Read-only Agent Skill audit of requested app capabilities, least privilege rules, negative test cases and human approval checkpoint.

stories.headline: ShipStation's Slack helpdesk shows how agents can escalate safely
stories.read_scope: Full AWS case study: Deckhand Slack interface, scoped retrieval, screenshot input, Jira escalation, user confirmation and vendor-reported statistics.
stories.summary: AWS describes ShipStation Global's Deckhand helpdesk agent in Slack, combining permission-scoped knowledge retrieval, screenshot analysis and Jira ticket escalation. The case study reports message volume and user feedback from an early deployment; a high reply rate must not be mistaken for resolution. Ticket creation requires an explicit user selection and downstream validation.
stories.why_it_matters: Small teams can adapt this pattern by letting agents answer approved questions while reserving account changes and tickets for confirmation. Test private-document access, unanswered questions and escalation evidence before deployment. Evaluate user outcomes rather than headline response rates.
stories.image_alt_intent: Role-scoped Slack helpdesk retrieval with screenshots, uncertain-answer escalation, human-confirmed Jira ticket and audit receipt.
